claim: PR #20 verifier authenticated comment/reply identity but did not bind claim-bearing finding/reply semantics strongly enough.
basis: Confirmed by development adjudication and the accepted PR #20 remediation that added exact body/update bindings and negative semantic regressions.

claim: Executable prevention references were accepted from checkout filesystem state instead of tracked regular files in the exact Git tree.
basis: Confirmed by development reproduction; remediation moved repository reference authority to git ls-tree HEAD and added .git/untracked/staged/symlink regressions.

claim: The cross-chat repeat-prevention process was normatively duplicated across DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL and a second mutable document.
basis: Confirmed against immutable BASE ownership rules; remediation restored DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL as sole normative owner and made the second document explanatory only.

claim: BOUNDED_FOLLOW_UP accepted arbitrary non-empty strings rather than recoverable durable locators.
basis: Confirmed by direct validator reproduction; remediation constrained locator syntax/authority and added negative regressions.

claim: UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS could coexist with an apparently complete search state and disappear from startup visibility.
basis: Confirmed by direct validator/summary reproduction; remediation made pending analysis bounded and visible, then later strengthened retirement handling.

claim: The explanatory repeat-prevention document still duplicated mutable live registry inventory despite no longer being a normative owner.
basis: Confirmed by direct document review; remediation removed copied live pattern state and added a regression that keeps the explanatory page pointer-only.

claim: A RETIRED top-level status could hide unresolved BOUNDED_FOLLOW_UP or UNKNOWN_PENDING_ANALYSIS state from active retrieval.
basis: Confirmed by direct validator reproduction; remediation prohibited retirement while unresolved debt remains and classified the recurrence as DFP-0006-O002 / GUARD_TOO_NARROW.

claim: PROCESS_INCIDENT authority accepted a generic owner-authored comment marker plus occurrence SHA without binding the source comment update identity/body digest or the claimed failure class and exact occurrence tuple.
basis: Confirmed by direct inspection of the exact-head authority verifier and the current P1 review finding; remediation adds exact non-HEAD process-incident manifest binding, source body/update verification, and claim-specific occurrence mapping.

claim: The proposed historical paired-review prototype hid expected finding text from the skill but did not freeze reviewer-visible evidence, so post-target public comments, later fixes, or dispositions could reveal the answer key and invalidate blind evaluation.
basis: Confirmed against the proposed PR #23 controls and the already-accepted research leakage rule in SEMANTIC_REVIEWER_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN.md; remediation requires identical pre-target evidence snapshots for both arms, excludes post-target evidence, records leakage, and invalidates leaked cases for Gate OK1.

claim: The research provenance candidate allowed documentation, paper, service, or API evidence to be represented by mutable URLs and nominal versions without binding the exact content that was verified.
basis: Confirmed by direct inspection of the PR #23 provenance candidate; remediation requires every retained evidence item to carry an immutable revision, immutable snapshot reference, or cryptographic content digest and fails closed when exact content cannot be re-resolved.

claim: The PR #23 acceptance chronology in EVIDENCE_INDEX conflated the merge precondition expected_head_sha with the resulting merge commit, making immutable acceptance identity contradictory.
basis: Confirmed against the accepted PR #23 exact source HEAD and merge commit. Remediation separates expected_head_sha=90b533fd1f2de743dfe388fc1e9747658039f1e1 from resulting merge commit c673c11bd0490b3b8218a11173e30c90d5b783a0 and adds a repository guard against future accepted-head/expected-head divergence in EVIDENCE_INDEX.

claim: The semantic-binding layer could silently drop a required claim-bearing comment when its registry repository/PR identity drifted, because selection happened before completeness enforcement and zero selected bindings were accepted.
basis: Confirmed by direct inspection of records_for(), validate_snapshot(), the accepted reconciliation wrapper, and the comment-id-only completeness regression on PR #26 HEAD 7058c8ed. Remediation requires exact role/repository/PR/surface/comment coverage and fail-closed required selection before claim-bearing reconciliation can proceed.

claim: PR #26 duplicated the canonical F055/F056 updated_at and body-digest evidence facts into the new semantic-binding registry even though the accepted authority-CI reconciliation already owns and verifies those facts.
basis: Confirmed against data/bootstrap-commentary-authority-ci-reconciliation.json and its accepted verifier. Remediation removes those mutable facts from the new direct registry and derives effective F055/F056 semantic bindings from the existing canonical authority-CI record instead.

claim: The DFP-0001 transition to repository_search=COMPLETED left development-failure-pattern unit fixtures and assertions bound to the former bounded-follow-up state, causing the required unit gate to fail.
basis: Confirmed by the exact review finding and reproduced CI failures. The remediation updated the existing development-failure-pattern fixtures/assertions to reflect the completed DFP-0001 state while preserving bounded-follow-up coverage on an appropriate fixture. This is a CI-blocking test-maintenance defect associated with the governed state transition, not evidence of a distinct durable failure mechanism requiring a new DFP identity.

claim: DFP-0003 searched_scope referenced a non-existent hyphenated semantic-binding test path instead of the tracked underscore-named file, so the exact-HEAD registry validator correctly rejected the PR.
basis: Confirmed by the exact review finding and CI #210 registry-validation failure. Remediation changed only the locator to tests/test_bootstrap_commentary_semantic_bindings.py. The existing tracked-regular-file validation guard detected the bad reference before acceptance, so this is not a recurrence of repository.reference_not_git_bound and does not create a new durable failure-pattern identity.

claim: The new surface-drift regression expected the family-coverage error even though the deliberately malformed issue-comment record correctly failed earlier on forbidden review-thread fields, making the required unit suite fail despite fail-closed production behavior.
basis: Confirmed by the exact review finding and CI #211 unit failure. Remediation keeps the earlier fail-closed validation and changes only the test expectation for the surface mutation; all other tuple-drift cases continue to require family-coverage failure. This is a regression-test expectation defect, not a distinct production failure mechanism requiring a new DFP identity.

claim: The PR #26 acceptance chronology in docs/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md grouped DFA-0014 as a later finding after the 7058c8ed fresh review even though DFA-0014 is bound to source HEAD ca67eb94332106e59471b281b84c09dbbbadb11d, which precedes 7058c8ed84f48ac7e3192e41af55ee9f838a665a in PR #26 history.
basis: Confirmed against the exact DFA-0014 adjudication record and PR #26 Git ancestry. Remediation splits DFA-0014 into its actual earlier chronology position and leaves DFA-0015/DFA-0016 after the 7058 fresh-review step. This exposes a distinct evidence-index chronology-ordering mechanism rather than the accepted-head/merge-role conflation covered by DFP-0009.

claim: Intermediate HEAD 399d0efb still carried the already-open PR #26 chronology-order defect.
basis: Corroborates DFP-0010 before its remediation completed; no new occurrence.

claim: The new chronology guard omitted middle adjudications from compact DFA ranges.
basis: Confirmed while DFP-0010 prevention was still unaccepted; strengthen that same guard by expanding ranges before ancestry checks. No new pattern or post-prevention occurrence.

claim: The chronology guard treated repeated summary-range references as fresh events and falsely reversed chronology.
basis: Confirmed by CI #223 while DFP-0010 prevention was still unaccepted; strengthen the same guard by per-block first-occurrence event semantics after full range expansion. No new pattern or post-prevention occurrence.

claim: The intermediate chronology guard only parsed DFA references from numbered-item first lines and could miss references placed on continuation lines.
basis: Confirmed on intermediate HEAD 157442562dd14a8811032096f95e543476f575f3. Current remediation already accumulates the complete numbered event text before extracting DFA references. This occurred while DFP-0010 prevention was still unaccepted, so it strengthens the same guard and is not a post-prevention recurrence or a new pattern.

claim: The chronology guard ordered only DFA-bearing events, so a descendant exact-HEAD review event without a DFA could be followed by an older DFA-bearing source HEAD without detection.
basis: Confirmed on exact HEAD 658ad589b18c2dd45fb8889c87ee60b7f8e3f42c. Remediation must include explicit event HEAD identities from every numbered chronology item, not only DFA-derived heads, while preserving per-source-PR ancestry checking. This finding occurred before DFP-0010 prevention received terminal acceptance, so it strengthens the same guard rather than creating a new pattern or repeat occurrence.

claim: The chronology guard collected explicit HEAD references before DFA-derived source heads inside the same numbered event, so it could reverse valid textual order and produce a false chronology failure.
basis: Confirmed against exact review comment 3966395985 on source HEAD f96f41bb7ed26329030afe1b00349d233b777927. Remediation preserves interleaved DFA/HEAD textual order within each numbered event while retaining per-source-PR ancestry checks. The finding occurred before DFP-0010 prevention received terminal acceptance, so it strengthens that same guard and is not a post-prevention recurrence or a new pattern.

claim: The chronology parser kept appending ordinary top-level prose to the final numbered event after the numbered chronology had ended, so unrelated trailing HEAD references could create false ancestry failures.
basis: Confirmed against exact review comment 3967003930. Remediation preserves indented continuation lines but terminates the chronology list when ordinary non-indented top-level prose begins after a numbered event. The finding occurred before DFP-0010 prevention received terminal acceptance, so it strengthens the same guard and is not a post-prevention recurrence or a new pattern.

claim: The chronology guard assigned explicit HEAD references to a source PR from surrounding DFA context but did not verify that the explicit HEAD was reachable from that PR's refs/pull/<pr>/head, allowing an available descendant commit outside the source PR to be accepted as that PR's chronology HEAD.
basis: Confirmed by independent code inspection after the fresh ordinary-Chat FINDINGS result. On exact HEAD 12a1b4885280add3877237fc018b72d1a1883276, ensure_source_history() returns early when SHAs are already available and is_ancestor() checks only commit ancestry; assert_chronology_order() therefore lacks explicit source-PR membership validation. Remediation must fetch/resolve the exact source PR head, require explicit HEAD reachability from it, and add a negative regression using an available descendant commit outside the source PR. DFP-0010 prevention is still unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence or new DFP identity.

claim: The chronology guard failed to recognize the established prefixed heading form such as `#### PR #9 review/remediation chronology`, so a DFA-bearing chronology block using that canonical style could be omitted from ancestry validation while another governed block kept the overall guard nonempty.
basis: Confirmed against exact PR #27 HEAD 482d4f35efd0ead0f74961901777e00723f30fd5 and docs/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md, which already contains prefixed lowercase review/remediation chronology headings. Remediation must recognize the established optional `PR #<n>` prefix case-insensitively and add a regression proving a reversed DFA chronology under the prefixed heading is governed and rejected. DFP-0010 prevention is still unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence or new DFP identity.

claim: The chronology parser accepted only dot-delimited ordered-list markers, so valid parenthesis-delimited numbered chronology items could be silently skipped and a reversed DFA chronology could evade the DFP-0010 ancestry guard.
basis: Confirmed from the fresh ordinary-Chat review handoff on exact HEAD fc1c08d233c9a0be560f34e097fcfe3c3c46d3be. Remediation must recognize CommonMark-style one-to-nine-digit ordered-list markers using `.` or `)` with bounded following whitespace and include a negative regression proving reversed `)` chronology is parsed and rejected. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence or new DFP identity.

claim: The chronology heading recognizer omitted valid ATX headings with an optional closing hash sequence, allowing a DFA-bearing chronology under such a heading to be silently skipped while another governed block kept the global assertion nonempty.
basis: Confirmed from the fresh ordinary-Chat review handoff on exact HEAD fc1c08d233c9a0be560f34e097fcfe3c3c46d3be. Remediation must recognize the valid optional ATX closing hash sequence without weakening the established optional PR prefix and case-insensitive matching, and add a reversed-chronology regression using a closing-hash heading. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence or new DFP identity.

claim: The source-PR membership guard resolved mutable `refs/pull/<pr>/head` instead of the immutable accepted exact PR HEAD, so later movement of a source pull ref could change validation authority for unchanged canonical chronology.
basis: Confirmed from the durable handoff of live Codex review comment 3970052851 on exact HEAD fc1c08d233c9a0be560f34e097fcfe3c3c46d3be. This is the same still-unaccepted DFP-0010 prevention surface already strengthened by DFA-0025: remediation must derive the immutable accepted source PR HEAD from canonical EVIDENCE_INDEX evidence, fetch that exact SHA rather than resolving the mutable pull ref, and add regression coverage proving the live pull-ref path is not authority.

claim: The immutable accepted-head parser rejected canonical `PR #N — <title>` context lines because its PR-context regex ended immediately after the em dash, so accepted-head binding failed closed for the real Evidence Index shape and blocked the chronology test suite.
basis: Confirmed by exact-head CI #243 unit job 102767232164 on e9317648d98f72202a32c6d44ec844327c97abe9. Registry validation passed, while all affected chronology tests failed at accepted_pr_heads() before ancestry evaluation. Remediation must accept title text after the canonical em dash while preserving exact PR-number capture and add a focused regression for the real acceptance-section shape. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this is another strengthening of the same guard rather than a post-prevention recurrence or new DFP identity.

claim: The chronology parser treated fenced Markdown examples as authoritative rendered chronology because it did not track code-fence state, allowing non-authoritative example headings/events to trigger false ancestry or unknown-adjudication failures.
basis: Confirmed against exact PR #27 HEAD 219541e45f59a62cf7e4901eb37b25309be4b4a4 and review comment 3976209327. Remediation must exclude fenced Markdown blocks before both chronology parsing and accepted-head extraction, preserve ordinary rendered chronology behavior, and add regressions for backtick and tilde fences. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence or new DFP identity.

claim: The chronology parser still treated HTML-commented and top-level four-space-indented Markdown examples as rendered canonical chronology because visible_markdown_lines() filtered fenced blocks only.
basis: Confirmed against exact PR #27 HEAD 27744a3db465c440c0632bac15e75162f94aae9b and review comment 3976541892. Remediation must exclude HTML-comment regions and top-level indented-code chronology examples before both chronology parsing and accepted-head extraction while preserving legitimate indented continuation content inside a rendered numbered chronology item, and add focused regressions for both non-rendered forms. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence or new DFP identity.

claim: Inline-code literals containing HTML comment delimiters can corrupt lexical comment state and hide a rendered reversed chronology event.
basis: Confirmed from fresh independent ordinary-Chat review of exact PR #27 HEAD 56a86c9f321f59aba6de5aaefeb8d528382f8952. Remediation must make HTML-comment exclusion aware of inline code spans so literal <!-- / --> inside rendered code cannot alter comment state, while genuine HTML comments remain excluded; add a reversed-chronology regression. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence.

claim: Fenced-code exclusion is not list-container-aware, so nested fenced examples can be absorbed as authoritative chronology continuation.
basis: Confirmed from fresh independent ordinary-Chat review of exact PR #27 HEAD 56a86c9f321f59aba6de5aaefeb8d528382f8952. Remediation must recognize backtick and tilde fences relative to a numbered list item's content indentation and exclude nested fenced contents while preserving legitimate indented continuation text; add regressions for nested fenced examples. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence.

claim: Raw-source chronology heading matching can miss a valid rendered ATX heading when inline emphasis formats its content, allowing a reversed block to escape validation.
basis: Confirmed from fresh independent ordinary-Chat review of exact PR #27 HEAD 56a86c9f321f59aba6de5aaefeb8d528382f8952. Remediation must derive chronology-heading identity from normalized rendered inline heading text or fail closed on applicable unrecognized forms, and add a reversed-order regression using emphasis-formatted heading content. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence.

claim: Fence markers inside real HTML comments can mutate fence state before comment exclusion and suppress later rendered chronology.
basis: Confirmed from live Codex review comment 3978886314 and durable owner handoff review_comment:3979047490 on exact PR #27 HEAD ca5a277d7770a1c9c2e639f3b79048d4dda2ca7a. Remediation adopts a stronger fail-closed canonical authority grammar: raw HTML/comment syntax is forbidden in docs/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md and guarded independently before chronology semantics can be accepted. A regression must prove an HTML comment containing an unmatched fence is rejected rather than allowed to hide later chronology. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence.

claim: Raw HTML blocks can expose non-rendered Markdown-looking chronology text to chronology authority.
basis: Confirmed from live Codex review comment 3978886321 and durable owner handoff review_comment:3979047496 on exact PR #27 HEAD ca5a277d7770a1c9c2e639f3b79048d4dda2ca7a. Remediation adopts a stronger fail-closed canonical authority grammar: raw HTML tags/blocks are forbidden in docs/EVIDENCE_INDEX.md and guarded independently, so raw HTML content cannot become chronology or accepted-head authority. A regression must reject a pre block containing fake DFA/HEAD chronology. DFP-0010 prevention remains unaccepted, so this strengthens the same guard rather than creating a post-prevention recurrence.
